hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane: $R + T\sin 60^\circ = 2.5(10)\cos 20^\circ$, giving $R = 25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ$.
For the least value of $T$, the particle is on the point of sliding down the plane, so friction $F = \mu R = 0.3R$ acts up the plane: $T\cos 60^\circ + 0.3R = 25\sin 20^\circ$.
For the greatest value of $T$, the particle is on the point of sliding up the plane, so friction $F = 0.3R$ acts down the plane: $T\cos 60^\circ = 25\sin 20^\circ + 0.3R$.
Solve each linear equation for $T$ using $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in equilibrium with mass $m = 2.5\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R + T\sin 60^\circ = 2.5g\cos 20^\circ = 25\cos 20^\circ$$
$$R = 25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ$$
State the limiting friction formula: $F = \mu R = 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ)$.

Case 1 (Least $T$): Impending motion is down the plane, so friction acts up the plane:
$$T\cos 60^\circ + F = 25\sin 20^\circ$$
$$T\cos 60^\circ + 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ$$
$$T(\cos 60^\circ - 0.3\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ - 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ)$$
$$T = \frac{25\sin 20^\circ - 7.5\cos 20^\circ}{\cos 60^\circ - 0.3\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{8.55050 - 7.04770}{0.5 - 0.25981} = \frac{1.50280}{0.24019} \approx 6.26\text{ N}$$

Case 2 (Greatest $T$): Impending motion is up the plane, so friction acts down the plane:
$$T\cos 60^\circ = 25\sin 20^\circ + F$$
$$T\cos 60^\circ = 25\sin 20^\circ + 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ)$$
$$T(\cos 60^\circ + 0.3\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ + 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ)$$
$$T = \frac{25\sin 20^\circ + 7.5\cos 20^\circ}{\cos 60^\circ + 0.3\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{8.55050 + 7.04770}{0.5 + 0.25981} = \frac{15.59820}{0.75981} \approx 20.5\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Sets up $R = 25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ$, forms $T\cos 60^\circ \pm 0.3R = 25\sin 20^\circ$, and finds least $T = 6.26\text{ N}$ and greatest $T = 20.5\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Set up axes parallel and perpendicular to the inclined plane. The plane is inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal. The gravitational weight is $W = mg = 2.5 \times 10 = 25\text{ N}$.

Resolve forces perpendicular to the plane in equilibrium:
$$\sum F_\perp = 0$$
$$R + T\sin 60^\circ - W\cos 20^\circ = 0$$
$$R = 25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ$$

State the limiting friction condition. In limiting equilibrium, the magnitude of friction is:
$$F = \mu R = 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ)$$

Determine the least value of $T$. When $T$ is minimal, the particle is on the verge of sliding downwards, so the friction force acts upwards along the incline:
$$\sum F_\parallel = 0$$
$$T\cos 60^\circ + F - W\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
$$T\cos 60^\circ + 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ$$
Expand and group the terms in $T$:
$$T\cos 60^\circ - 0.3T\sin 60^\circ = 25\sin 20^\circ - 7.5\cos 20^\circ$$
$$T(\cos 60^\circ - 0.3\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ - 7.5\cos 20^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$\cos 60^\circ - 0.3\sin 60^\circ = 0.5 - 0.3(0.866025) = 0.5 - 0.259808 = 0.240192$$
$$25\sin 20^\circ - 7.5\cos 20^\circ = 25(0.342020) - 7.5(0.939693) = 8.55050 - 7.04770 = 1.50280$$
$$T_{\text{least}} = \frac{1.50280}{0.240192} \approx 6.26\text{ N}$$

Determine the greatest value of $T$. When $T$ is maximal, the particle is on the verge of sliding upwards, so friction acts downwards along the incline:
$$T\cos 60^\circ - F - W\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
$$T\cos 60^\circ = 25\sin 20^\circ + 0.3(25\cos 20^\circ - T\sin 60^\circ)$$
$$T(\cos 60^\circ + 0.3\sin 60^\circ) = 25\sin 20^\circ + 7.5\cos 20^\circ$$
Substitute numerical values:
$$\cos 60^\circ + 0.3\sin 60^\circ = 0.5 + 0.259808 = 0.759808$$
$$25\sin 20^\circ + 7.5\cos 20^\circ = 8.55050 + 7.04770 = 15.59820$$
$$T_{\text{greatest}} = \frac{15.59820}{0.759808} \approx 20.5\text{ N}$$
